decision_basis.detail: Yang et al. (2026), arXiv:2607.08535, already studies fixed-output measurement changes under evaluator replacement across four judgment datasets and requires protocol audit trails. A FLAWS-only application is not a sufficient residual contribution.

The reference and proposed primary conditions simultaneously change truth granularity, lexical implementation, judge lineage, and aggregation, so a difference cannot be attributed to evaluator replacement.
The proposed request batches five anonymized system outputs together, whereas the released evaluator judges one identification model at a time. This adds an uncontrolled context intervention.
The frozen fixed-intercept logistic MLE separates at k=1 on the released rows after the declared same-model exclusions, blocking the adjusted rankings required by the hypotheses.
The paper-versus-code discrepancy changes 8 of 575 cells, below the frozen 5 percent materiality threshold, while the larger context-granularity effect does not establish evaluator validity.
The 115-instance public extension has no released instance-level human labels, preventing claims that a replacement judge or aggregation rule is more valid.

repair_decision.reason: A factorial redesign, three complete repeats, a new estimable ranking model, and human adjudication would still leave the central evaluator-replacement question substantially absorbed by newer work. The expected workshop value does not justify that budget.

next_action: Return to the governed topic portfolio, absorb the newly discovered prior, and select a locally testable candidate with a distinct research object, intervention, evaluation unit, and claim.
